name: LPN-to-ADN Transition (A45110, accelerated bridge)
sourceWorkbook: Southeastern CC: what the nursing dean and director told the owner on 2026-10-28 (sequence, eight-week sessions, rotations, group sizes, the NUR 111 lab split, the preceptorship, class size, workload); the ADN and LPN-to-ADN admission pages, the Nursing program page, the campus facilities list, the 2026–27 academic calendar, the NC Board of Nursing 2024 approved-programs list (140 students at one time) and 2021–2023 pass rates; course hours and credits from the NCCCS A45110 standard — compiled 2026-10-28
maxCohortNote: Class size 20 — the program admitted 20 to the inaugural Summer 2026 cohort after planning 10 and doubling on the applicant pool (2026-10-28); the number moves with second-year retention and applications, within the Board's 140 students at one time. The Fall 2026 schedule lists the transition course as NUR 221; its code, term and dates come with the Dec 4 sequence document (the pack keeps NUR 214 as the workspace carries it, and places the second-year courses as the ADN's standard sequence did until then).
weeklyHoursNote: Term hours per student are the catalog's weekly contact hours × 16 (the 16-week basis), whatever the term's length: the sessions carry them, the posted days, times and rooms place them. Hours and credits are the NCCCS course standard's. The program runs every NUR course but 111 and 213 as an eight-week session (A-Term / B-Term in fall and spring; the eight-week summer session from Jun 1 inside the college's 10-week term, May 17 – Jul 27, 2027), so those courses' sessions sit in eight of the term's weeks at twice the catalog's weekly hours. Days and times beyond NUR 111's Tuesday lab, Thursday lab sections and Wednesday clinical come with the Fall 2026 schedule (due Dec 4).

courses.title: Nursing Transition Concepts
courses.requisites: Admission to the LPN-to-ADN Transition (current unencumbered NC or compact LPN license, GPA ≥ 2.0, ATI Comprehensive Predictor)
courses.description: The bridge: concepts within the three domains of the individual, healthcare and nursing as the LPN moves to the RN role — evidence-based practice, quality improvement, communication, safety, the interdisciplinary team, informatics, assessment, clinical decision-making and professional behaviors. Completion carries the block credit for NUR 111, 112, 113 and 114 as the NCCCS transition design has it. Hours as the workspace's transition curriculum carries them (3-3-6); the program's Fall 2026 schedule lists the transition course as NUR 221, and its code, hours, term and dates come with the Dec 4 sequence document. Clinical on hospital medical-surgical units. Hours and credits are the NCCCS standard's; the term placement is the program's own (stated 2026-10-28) — the course-sequence document due Dec 4 confirms it.

courses.title: Complex Health Concepts
courses.requisites: NUR 111; NUR 112, 113, 114, 211 and 212 prior or concurrent
courses.description: Capstone: fluid/electrolytes, metabolism, perfusion, mobility, stress/coping, violence, health-wellness-illness, professional behaviors, caring interventions, managing care, healthcare systems and quality improvement; NCLEX-RN eligibility on completion. Sixteen weeks. The focused-client-care preceptorship: 240 clinical hours as fifteen 12-hour shifts 1:1 with a hospital RN the program assigns (two years' experience required; the student works the nurse's schedule over the placement window) plus 60 hours in the simulation lab; one faculty member oversees up to fifteen preceptorship students. The LPN-to-ADN cohort joins the second-year class. Hours and credits are the NCCCS standard's; the term placement is the program's own (stated 2026-10-28) — the course-sequence document due Dec 4 confirms it.
